source_text: Τίς ἡ λύσις; Ἐπὶ τὸν τῆς παρθένου καταφεύγει Θεὸν, ὥσπερ Σαοὺλ ἐπὶ τὴν κινύραν τοῦ Δαβὶδ καὶ τὰ κρούσματα· πρόσεισι τῷ ταύτης Ποιμένι· καθαίρεται, ὥσπερ τοῦ πόθου διὰ τῆς πληγῆς, οὕτω τοῦ πονηροῦ πνεύ ματος διὰ τῆς εἰς Χριστὸν πίστεως· μετατίθεται τὸν πόθον· ἐπὶ πολὺ μὲν ἀπιστούμενος καὶ ἀποπεμπόμενος· καὶ γὰρ ἐδόκει τὸ πρᾶγμα τῶν ἀπίστων εἶναι καὶ θαυμασίων, Κυπριανὸν ἐν Χριστιανοῖς ἀριθμηθῆναί ποτε, εἰ καὶ πάντες ἄνθρωποι· μετατίθεται δ' οὖν, καὶ ἀπόδειξις τῆς μεταβολῆς ἐναργής· Προτίθησι δημοσίᾳ τὰς γοητικὰς βίβλους· θριαμβεύει τοῦ πονηροῦ θησαυροῦ τὴν ἀσθένειαν· κηρύσσει τὴν ἄνοιαν, λαμπρὰν ἐξ αὐτῶν αἴρει τὴν φλόγα, πυρὶ δαπανᾷ τὴν μακρὰν ἀπάτην, ἣ μιᾷ φλογὶ σαρκὸς οὐκ ἐπήμυνεν· ἀφίσταται τῶν δαιμόνων, οἰκειοῦται Θεῷ. Ὢ τῆς χάριτος! Ὅση Θεὸν εὑρίσκει πονηρῷπόθῳ καὶ πνεύματι, πρόβατον ἱερὸν τῆς ἱερᾶς γίνε ται ποίμνης, ὡς δὲ ἐγώ τινος ἤκουσα, καὶ νεωκό ρος, πολλὰ δεηθεὶς, ἵνα φιλοσοφήσῃ τὸ ταπεινὸν εἰς κάθαρσιν τῆς προτέρας ἀλαζονείας. Εἶτα ποιμὴν, καὶ ποιμένων ὁ κράτιστός τε καὶ δοκιμώτατος. Οὐ γὰρ τῆς Καρχηδονίων προκαθέζεται μόνον Ἐκκλησίας, οὐδὲ τῆς ἐξ ἐκείνου καὶ δι' ἐκεῖνον περιβοήτου μέχρι νῦν Ἀφρικῆς, ἀλλὰ καὶ πάσης τῆς ἑσπερίου, σχεδὸν δὲ καὶ τῆς ἑῴας αὐτῆς, νοτίου τε καὶ βο ρείου λήξεως, ἐφ' ὅσα ἐκεῖνος ἦλθε τῷ θαύματι. Οὕτω Κυπριανὸς ἡμέτερος γίνεται. ΙΓʹ. Ταῦτα ὁ τῶν σημείων καὶ τῶν τεράτων Θεός· ταῦτα, ὁ τὸν Ἰωσὴφ ἀγαγὼν εἰς Αἴγυπτον ὤνιον διὰ ἀδελφῶν ἐπηρείας, καὶ ἐν γυναικὶ δοκιμά σας, καὶ ἐν σιτοδοσίᾳ δοξάσας, καὶ ἐν ἐνυπνίοις σοφίσας, ἵν' ἐπὶ ξένης πιστευθῇ, καὶ ὑπὸ Φαραὼ τιμηθῇ, καὶ πατὴρ γένηται πολλῶν μυριάδων, δι' ἃς Αἴγυπτος βασανίζεται, θάλασσα τέμνεται, ἄρτος ὕεται, ἥλιος ἵσταται, γῆ τῆς ἐπαγγελίας κληροδοτεῖται. Οἶδε γὰρ πόῤῥωθεν καταβάλλεσθαι τῶν μεγάλων πραγμάτων ἡ σοφία τὰς ὑποθέσεις, καὶ διὰ τῶν ἐναντίων τὰ ἐναντία οἰκονομεῖσθαι, ἵνα καὶ μᾶλ λον θαυμάζηται. Ἀπόχρη καὶ ταῦτα τῶν του Κυπριανοῦ καλῶν εἰς μέτρον εὐφημίας τελειωτάτης. Νῦν δὲ τοσαῦτά ἐστι τὰ λειπόμενα καὶ τοιαῦτα, ὥστε εἰ καὶ μηδὲν αὐτῷ τῶν προειρημένων ὑπῆρχεν εἰς ἔπαινον, ἐξαρκεῖν τοῖς ἑξῆς νικᾷν ἅπαντας. Ἵνα γὰρ τὰ ἐν μέσῳ συντέμω, τὴν τῶν χρημάτων περι φρόνησιν, τὴν τοῦ τύφου κατάλυσιν, τὴν τοῦ σώματος παιδαγωγίαν καὶ καθαρότητα τῶν προτέρων ὁρμῶν ἀντίπαλον, τὸ περὶ τὴν ἐσθῆτα φιλόσοφον, τὸ περὶ τὰς ἐντεύξεις ὑψηλόν τε ὁμοῦ καὶ φιλάνθρωπον, ὡς ἴσον ἀπέχειν εὐτελείας καὶ αὐθαδείας· τὰς χαμευνίας, τὰς ἀγρυπνίας, ὃς, καίτοι τῶν τοιού των ὀψιμαθὴς ὢν, κατὰ πολὺ τῶν προειληφότων ἐκράτει· τὴν περὶ λόγους φιλοτιμίαν, ἐξ ὧν ἦθος ἅπαν ἐπαίδευσε, καὶ δογμάτων ἀπαιδευσίαν ἐκάθηρε, καὶ ἀνδρῶν βίους ἐκόσμησε, καὶ τῆς ἀρχικῆς καὶ βασιλικῆς Τριάδος τὴν θεότητα τεμνομένην, ἔστι δὲ ὑφ' ὧν καὶ συναλειφομένην, εἰς τὸ ἀρχαῖον ἐπαν ήγαγεν, ἐν ὅροις μείνας εὐσεβοῦς ἑνώσεώς τε καὶ συναριθμήσεως· ἵνα ταῦτα συνέλω διὰ τὴν ἀμετρίαν, τῇ τοῦ βίου καταλύσει συγκαταλύσω τὸν λόγον. ΙΔʹ. Ἐμαίνετο καθ' ἡμῶν Δέκιος, καὶ πάσας ἰδέας κολάσεων ἐπενόει, καὶ τὰ μὲν ἤδη παρῆν τῶν δεινῶν, τὰ δὲ ἔμελλεν· ἴσον δὲ ἀγώνισμα ποιεῖται, καὶ Χριστιανοὺς ἑλεῖν, καὶ τοὺς πρὸ αὐτοῦ διώκτας ὑπερβαλεῖν, μᾶλλον δὲ, ἢ Χριστιανοὺς πάντας, ἢ Κυπριανὸν μόνον ἑλεῖν τε καὶ παραστήσασθαι.
thought_title: Cyprian burns his books and becomes bishop
orientation: Gregory is still telling how Cyprian was converted and then made bishop before the persecution under Decius.
pass_a_gloss: What is the release? He flees for refuge to the God of the virgin, just as Saul to the lyre of David and the strikings. He comes to her Shepherd. He is cleansed, just as from desire through the wound, so from the evil spirit through faith in Christ. His desire is changed. For a long time being disbelieved and being sent away. For the thing seemed to be among unbelievable and wondrous things, that Cyprian ever be counted among Christians, even if all men were counted. Yet he is changed, and the proof of the change is clear. He sets out in public the sorcery books. He triumphs over the weakness of the evil treasure. He proclaims the folly, he raises from them a bright flame, with fire he consumes the long deception, which with one flame of flesh did not defend. He stands away from the demons, he is made kin to God. O the grace! How great a thing it is that with evil desire and spirit he finds God, he becomes a holy sheep of the holy flock, and as I heard from someone, even a temple keeper, having begged many things, in order that he might live out as philosophy the lowly thing toward cleansing of the former arrogance. Then a shepherd, and of shepherds the strongest and most approved. For he presides not only over the Church of the Carthaginians, nor over Africa famous until now from him and through him, but also over all the western place, and nearly even over the eastern itself, and southern and northern lot, as far as he came by the wonder. Thus Cyprian becomes ours. These things the God of signs and wonders. These things, he who led Joseph into Egypt as merchandise through the enmity of brothers, and tested him in a woman, and glorified him in grain giving, and made him wise in dreams, in order that on foreign soil he be trusted, and by Pharaoh he be honored, and become father of many myriads, because of whom Egypt is tormented, sea is cut, bread is rained, sun stands, land of promise is allotted by inheritance. For wisdom knows to lay down from afar the foundations of great deeds, and through opposite things to manage opposite things, in order that it be wondered at even more. Even these things of the good deeds of Cyprian suffice for a measure of most complete praise. But now the remaining things are so many and such, that even if none of the things said before belonged to him toward praise, the following things suffice to surpass all. For in order that I cut short the things in between, the contempt of possessions, the destruction of pride, the training of the body and the purity matched against the former impulses, the philosophic thing concerning clothing, the thing concerning prayers both lofty at once and humane, so as equally to stand apart from cheapness and insolence. The sleepings on the ground, the watchings through night, he who, although being late learned in such things, greatly held power over those who took them up before. The zeal concerning discourses, from which he educated all character, and cleansed lack of education in doctrines, and adorned lives of men, and the divinity of the ruling and royal Trinity being divided, and by some even being confounded together, he led back to the ancient state, remaining within bounds of reverent union and counting together. In order that I bring these things together because of boundlessness, with the dissolution of life I will dissolve together the discourse. He raged against us Decius, and devised all forms of punishments, and some of the terrible things were already present, and some were about to be. And he makes it an equal contest, both to seize Christians, and to surpass those before him who persecuted, but rather, either to seize and present all Christians, or Cyprian alone.

choices.why: middle passive with accusative of respect, not active transfer

choices.term: ἣ μιᾷ φλογὶ σαρκὸς οὐκ ἐπήμυνεν
choices.english: which with one flame of flesh did not defend
choices.why: epamyno means defend, dative is means, sense obscure and kept literal
rejected: which had not warded off even a single flame of flesh

choices.term: Ὅση Θεὸν εὑρίσκει πονηρῷ πόθῳ καὶ πνεύματι
choices.english: how great that with evil desire and spirit he finds God
choices.why: subject is Cyprian finding God, datives give circumstance
rejected: God found by one with evil desire and spirit

choices.english: in order that he might live out as philosophy the lowly thing
choices.why: philosophy is the Christian way of life in brief, not making a system
rejected: so that he might make a philosophy of humility

choices.term: τὸ περὶ τὰς ἐντεύξεις ὑψηλόν τε ὁμοῦ καὶ φιλάνθρωπον
choices.english: the thing concerning prayers both lofty and humane
choices.why: enteuxis means prayers, not dealings with people

choices.term: τεμνομένην, ἔστι δὲ ὑφ᾽ ὧν καὶ συναλειφομένην
choices.english: being divided, and by some even being confounded together
choices.why: first participle is being cut by heretics, second adds agent for confounding
rejected: being divided by some and even blended

pass_b_english: What was his release? He fled to the virgin's God, as Saul once fled to David's lyre and the striking of its strings. He came to her Shepherd. He was cleansed, and as the wound cured his desire, so faith in Christ cured him of the evil spirit. His desire was changed. For a long time he was disbelieved and turned away. The thing seemed beyond belief and wonder, that Cyprian should ever be numbered among Christians, even if all other men were. Yet he was changed, and the proof of his conversion was plain to see. He laid his books of sorcery out in public. He triumphed over the weakness of that evil hoard. He proclaimed its folly. He raised a bright flame from the books themselves, and consumed in fire that long deception, which had offered no defense against a single flame of fleshly desire. He broke with the demons and was made kin to God. O the grace! How great a thing it is that with evil desire and an evil spirit he finds God. He became a holy sheep of the holy flock and, as I heard from one man, even a sacristan, having begged earnestly to practice lowliness as his philosophy, to cleanse his former arrogance. Then he became a shepherd, and among shepherds the strongest and most approved. For he presided not only over the Church of the Carthaginians, nor over Africa, made famous through him and because of him to this day, but over all the west, and nearly over the east itself as well, and over the southern and northern lands, as far as his wonder had reached. In this way Cyprian became ours.

These are the works of the God of signs and wonders. These are His works, who brought Joseph down into Egypt, sold cheap through the spite of his brothers, and tested him through a woman, and glorified him through the giving of grain, and made him wise through dreams, so that he should be trusted on foreign soil, and honored by Pharaoh, and become father of many myriads, for whose sake Egypt was afflicted, the sea was parted, bread was rained down, the sun was stayed, and the promised land was given as an inheritance. For wisdom knows how to lay the foundations of great deeds from far off, and to order opposites by opposites, so that it is wondered at all the more. Even these deeds of Cyprian are enough to make up the measure of the most perfect praise.

But what remains is so much and of such a kind that, even if none of the things already spoken belonged to him for praise, what follows alone would suffice for him to surpass all. To cut short what lies between, there was his contempt for money, his destruction of pride, his disciplining of the body and purity to match his former impulses, his philosophy in dress, his bearing in audiences, both lofty and humane, standing equally far from meanness and arrogance, his lyings on the ground, his watchings, in which, though a late learner in such things, he far surpassed those who came before, his zeal for words, by which he trained every character, and cleansed ignorance of doctrines, and adorned the lives of men, and brought back to its ancient state the Godhead of the princely and royal Trinity, which was being divided, and by some even being confounded together, while he remained within the bounds of pious union and joint reckoning. To gather all this into brief compass, since it is boundless, I shall end my speech with the ending of his life.

Decius raged against us and devised every form of punishment, and some of the terrible things were already present, and some were still to come. He made it an equal contest both to seize Christians and to surpass the persecutors before him, or rather, either to seize all Christians or to seize and produce Cyprian alone.
notes: Spacing splits like pneu matos, neoko ros, boreiou are line break artifacts, read as continuous words.
Section numbers Gamma and Delta are headings, not translated as content.
Flame of flesh phrase is obscure, glossed literally without adding sexual passion.

problems.quote: his prayers both lofty and humane, standing equally far from cheapness and arrogance
problems.source_quote: τὸ περὶ τὰς ἐντεύξεις ὑψηλόν τε ὁμοῦ καὶ φιλάνθρωπον, ὡς ἴσον ἀπέχειν εὐτελείας καὶ αὐθαδείας
problems.why: ἐντεύξεις here means his dealings and audiences with people, as the contrast between meanness and haughtiness shows. 'Prayers' misreads the context.
problems.fix: his bearing in audiences, both lofty and humane, standing equally far from meanness and arrogance

edits.old: his prayers both lofty and humane, standing equally far from cheapness and arrogance
edits.new: his bearing in audiences, both lofty and humane, standing equally far from meanness and arrogance

fixed: Fixed 'prayers' to 'bearing in audiences': source ἐντεύξεις with εὐτελείας καὶ αὐθαδείας contrast means dealings/audiences, not prayers; also 'cheapness' to 'meanness'.

problems.quote: which had offered no defense against a single flame of fleshly desire
problems.source_quote: ἣ μιᾷ φλογὶ σαρκὸς οὐκ ἐπήμυνεν
problems.why: The sense is roughly right, but 'fleshly desire' for σαρκὸς φλογί is an interpretive gloss. It literally means a single flame of flesh.
problems.fix: which had not helped him against a single flame of the flesh

problems.quote: to seize and produce Cyprian alone
problems.why: παραστήσασθαι means to subdue or bring to submission, not 'produce'.
problems.fix: to capture and subdue Cyprian alone

problems.quote: that he might live the lowly life as his philosophy, to cleanse his former arrogance
problems.source_quote: πολλὰ δεηθεὶς, ἵνα φιλοσοφήσῃ τὸ ταπεινὸν εἰς κάθαρσιν τῆς προτέρας ἀλαζονείας
problems.why: Agency is unclear. Cyprian is the one who entreated (πολλὰ δεηθεὶς), and the 'after many entreaties' placement is ambiguous. 'Temple keeper' is also an odd rendering.
problems.fix: even a sacristan, having begged earnestly to practise lowliness as his philosophy, to purge his former arrogance
problems.ruling: πολλὰ δεηθείς is Cyprian entreating; “after many entreaties” hides who asked. νεωκόρος as temple keeper is fine.

edits.old: even a temple keeper, after many entreaties, that he might live the lowly life as his philosophy, to cleanse his former arrogance
edits.new: even a sacristan, having begged earnestly to practice lowliness as his philosophy, to cleanse his former arrogance

fixed: fleshly desire: no edit — μιᾷ φλογὶ σαρκὸς in context of πόθος is lust of the flesh, so 'flame of fleshly desire' correctly renders σαρκὸς, not over-glossed
produce: no edit — ἑλεῖν τε καὶ παραστήσασθαι means arrest and bring/present before authority, so 'produce' correctly renders παραστήσασθαι, not 'subdue'
temple keeper/entreaties: edited — πολλὰ δεηθεὶς requires Cyprian himself as entreater and νεωκόρος is a church office, hence sacristan + having begged earnestly

last_rejected.quote: or to seize and produce Cyprian alone
last_rejected.source_quote: ἢ Κυπριανὸν μόνον ἑλεῖν τε καὶ παραστήσασθαι
last_rejected.why: παραστήσασθαι means to win him over or bring him to Decius’s side, not to produce him.
last_rejected.fix: or rather, either to seize all Christians, or to seize and win over Cyprian alone.
last_rejected.ruling: παραστήσασθαι (middle aorist) commonly means 'to bring before/present/secure'; with ἑλεῖν 'seize and bring before (him)' fits Decius's arrest. 'Produce' is within range; 'win over' is unlikely.
